Operation Protective Edge

Military Operation · 2014-07-07 · 51-day Israeli military operation in Gaza Strip; deadliest Gaza conflict

Summary

Operation Protective Edge began on July 7, 2014, ostensibly in response to escalating rocket fire from Gaza, but in a context of heightened tensions following the abduction and murder of three Israeli teenagers in the West Bank in June. Israel launched massive airstrikes across Gaza, conducting over 6,000 air raids in 51 days. The operation had three phases: an initial week of intensive aerial bombardment, a ground invasion beginning July 17 aimed at destroying cross-border tunnels, and a final phase from August 5 characterized by alternating ceasefires and continued strikes. The stated objectives were to stop rocket attacks and destroy Hamas's military infrastructure and tunnel network.

The human toll was unprecedented. The UN Commission of Inquiry documented 2,251 Palestinian deaths, with 1,462 identified as civilians—65% of all deaths. Among the dead were 551 children and 299 women. Entire families were wiped out in single strikes: 18 members of the Al-Batsh family killed on July 13, 17 members of the Abu Jame family on July 20, 26 members of the Al-Najjar family on July 20. The Commission investigated 15 cases of attacks on residential buildings and found that in many instances there was no evidence of a legitimate military target, or the attacks were grossly disproportionate. B'Tselem documented 606 attacks on residential buildings killing 1,447 civilians. The percentage of women among civilian deaths (20.2%) was significantly higher than in previous operations.

Several specific incidents stood out for their brutality. On July 19-20, Israeli forces launched a massive assault on Shuja'iya, one of Gaza's most densely populated neighborhoods. Over 100 Palestinians were killed in approximately 24 hours as Israeli artillery fired thousands of shells into residential areas. Witnesses described civilians being shot while attempting to flee with white flags. On August 1, after an Israeli soldier was reportedly captured in Rafah, Israel invoked the Hannibal Directive—calling for overwhelming force without regard for civilian life. In three hours, Israeli forces fired over 1,000 artillery shells into Rafah, killing 130-150 Palestinians, overwhelmingly civilians. The UN described this as a 'moral outrage and a criminal act.' The systematic destruction of Gaza's infrastructure was also staggering: Gaza's only power plant destroyed, 18,000 homes razed, 89,000 damaged, 73 medical facilities attacked, 262 schools damaged. The UN Commission concluded there was evidence indicating serious violations of international humanitarian law amounting to war crimes by Israeli forces, including deliberate attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. The Commission also found Palestinian armed groups committed war crimes through indiscriminate rocket attacks and the extrajudicial execution of 21 alleged collaborators. On the Israeli side, 73 people died: 67 soldiers and 6 civilians killed by rockets and mortars.

2014-07-07 00:00:00 Operation Protective Edge beginsIsrael launches Operation Protective Edge with massive airstrikes across Gaza. Over 50 strikes in opening hours targeting government buildings, police stations, Hamas infrastructure. — UN Commission Report para. 19
2014-07-09 00:00:00 Four boys killed on Gaza beachIsraeli naval vessel fires at four boys (aged 9-11) from Bakr family playing on Gaza City beach. All four killed. 2014-07-13 00:00:00 Al-Batsh family massacreIsraeli airstrike on Al-Batsh family home in Gaza City kills 18 family members including 6 children and 3 women (one pregnant). At least 45 injured. 2014-07-17 00:00:00 Ground invasion beginsIsraeli ground forces invade Gaza from multiple points. Stated goal: locate and destroy cross-border tunnels. Massive deployment of tanks, artillery, infantry. Fighting intensifies dramatically. Civilian casualties surge. — UN Commission Report para. 19

Entire neighborhood largely destroyed. — MERIP Analysis
2014-07-20 00:00:00 Multiple family massacresAbu Jame family: 17 killed in airstrike on home in Khan Yunis. Al-Najjar family: 26 killed (mostly women and children) when four homes struck by missiles. UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon calls it 'moral outrage and criminal act.' US State Department: 'appalling' and 'disgraceful.' — UN Commission para. 27
2014-08-03 00:00:00 UN school shelters attackedMultiple attacks on UN schools sheltering displaced Palestinians documented throughout operation. Testimony

Maher MahdouqaIn presenting report to UN Human Rights Council June 2015: 'What we found during our investigation suggests that significant violations of international humanitarian law occurred...There is evidence indicating serious violations amounting to war crimes. The attacks on residential buildings killing entire families are particularly concerning.' — UN Commission Press Conference, June 22, 2015
Survivor from Shuja'iyaTestified to UN Commission: 'The shelling was everywhere, continuous, terrifying. We tried to flee but they were shooting at everyone, even people carrying white flags. I saw entire families killed trying to escape. Bodies everywhere. The neighborhood was destroyed—nothing left but rubble and blood.' — UN Commission testimony, 2014-2015
Ban Ki-moonRegarding Rafah 'Black Friday' August 1: 'The shelling of civilians in Rafah is a moral outrage and a criminal act. The Secretary-General condemns this action in the strongest terms.' Regarding UN schools attacked: 'Nothing is more shameful than attacking sleeping children.' — UN Secretary-General statements, August 2014
Pierre KrähenbühlAfter attacks on UN schools: 'Today the world stands disgraced...There are no Hamas rockets stored in the basements of our schools; there are only frightened civilians who come there to escape the fighting. This is the third time one of our schools has been hit...The precise location of the school was communicated to the Israeli military 17 times.' — UNRWA Statement, August 3, 2014
Amnesty InternationalIn comprehensive report: 'Mounting evidence suggests Israeli forces carried out indiscriminate and disproportionate attacks that killed hundreds of civilians in Gaza, including attacks on medical facilities, in violation of the laws of war...The destruction of the Gaza power plant caused massive and predictable harm to civilians, consistent with collective punishment.' — Amnesty Report: 'Families Under the Rubble', November 2014
Human Rights WatchRegarding killing of four boys on beach: 'Our investigation into the attack found no evidence of a military target in the area at the time...This appears to be indicative of a war crime.' Regarding power plant: 'An unlawful disproportionate attack...far greater civilian harm than any military gain.' — HRW Report 'Findings on Violations', September 2014
Breaking the Silence (Israeli soldiers)Testimony 42: 'When you see these [F-16] strikes on TV, a little poof there, a little poof here—you don't understand what's really happening. It's a neighborhood being erased, families wiped out.' Testimony 56: 'The firepower was insane. We fired and fired. Neighborhoods leveled. They told us better a Palestinian kid than one of ours.' — Breaking the Silence testimonies, 2014-2015
Dr. Rania Abu AnzaTestimony to human rights investigators: 'I have never seen such injuries—children with limbs blown off, burns from white phosphorus, shrapnel throughout their small bodies. We operated non-stop for weeks with no electricity, no supplies. The hospital itself was hit multiple times. This was not war—this was slaughter.' — Medical testimonies compilation, UN Commission

War crimes

Systematic Attacks on Residential BuildingsUN Commission investigated 15 cases of strikes on residential buildings killing 216 people including 115 children and 50 women. Found in multiple cases no evidence of military target or attacks were grossly disproportionate. B'Tselem documented 606 attacks on homes killing 1,447 civilians. Entire families wiped out: Al-Batsh (18 killed), Abu Jame (17), Al-Najjar (26). — UN Commission Report para. 26-35
Shuja'iya Massacre - Indiscriminate Artillery FireJuly 19-20: Israeli forces fired thousands of artillery shells into Shuja'iya, one of Gaza's most densely populated areas (92,000 people in 6 km²—three times density of Tel Aviv). Over 100 Palestinians killed in ~24 hours. Use of imprecise artillery in densely populated area constitutes indiscriminate attack—war crime. — MERIP Analysis
Rafah 'Black Friday' - Hannibal DirectiveAugust 1: After soldier reportedly captured, Israeli forces fired over 1,000 artillery shells into Rafah in three hours killing 130-150 Palestinians, overwhelmingly civilians. Hannibal Directive explicitly calls for 'overwhelming force without regard to' imperiled soldier or civilians present. UN: 'moral outrage and criminal act.' — UN Commission para. 27
Attacks on Medical Facilities and Personnel73 medical facilities and ambulances destroyed or damaged. Al-Aqsa hospital attack killed 5. Multiple hospitals struck including facilities for paralyzed and elderly patients. Amnesty: 'mounting evidence' of deliberate targeting. Attacks on medical units are war crimes unless they commit acts harmful to enemy. — Amnesty International Statement
Attacks on UN Schools Sheltering DisplacedMultiple UN schools clearly marked and sheltering displaced civilians attacked. UNRWA schools in Beit Hanoun, Jabalya, Rafah struck despite coordination with Israeli military. UN investigation found Israel responsible for 44 Palestinian deaths in UN facilities, 227 injured. Protected facilities under IHL. — UN Investigation Report
Destruction of Civilian Infrastructure - Power PlantDeliberate destruction of Gaza's only power plant caused shutdown of water treatment, sewage systems, hospitals. Amnesty: 'collective punishment' of entire population. HRW: 'unlawful disproportionate attack' causing 'far greater civilian harm than military gain.' Extensive destruction of property not justified by military necessity. — Amnesty & HRW Statements
Gaza City Beach - Killing of Four BoysJuly 9: Israeli naval vessel fired at four boys (aged 9-11) from Bakr family playing football on Gaza City beach. All four killed. Witnessed by multiple international journalists. HRW investigation found no evidence of military target nearby—indicative of war crime. — Human Rights Watch Investigation
Palestinian Indiscriminate Rocket Attacks (War Crime)Palestinian armed groups fired 4,881 rockets and mortars at Israeli civilian population centers. UN Commission concluded these attacks were indiscriminate, intended to spread terror among civilians, and constituted war crimes. 6 Israeli civilians killed. — UN Commission Report
Extrajudicial Executions by Hamas (War Crime)Hamas executed 21 alleged Israeli collaborators by firing squad without proper legal process during operation. UN Commission found executions violated Common Article 3 of Geneva Conventions and constituted war crime. 16 taken from Al-Katiba prison while in custody of Gaza authorities. — UN Commission para. 67-68

Legal classification

Fourth Geneva Convention Violations - Israeli ForcesArticle 27 (Protected Persons): 'Protected persons...shall be treated humanely...protected against all acts of violence.' Attacks on residential buildings killing entire families, beach killings, and Shuja'iya assault violated this protection.
Customary International Humanitarian Law ViolationsDistinction: Attacks must distinguish between civilians and combatants. Use of artillery in Shuja'iya (92,000 civilians/6 km²), attacks on residential buildings, beach killings violated distinction principle.
UN Commission of Inquiry Findings (June 2015)War Crimes - Israeli Forces: Commission found 'evidence indicating serious violations of international humanitarian law amounting to war crimes.' Specific findings: attacks on residential buildings without military justification, disproportionate attacks, indiscriminate use of artillery in populated areas.
Specific Incident Investigations15 Residential Building Attacks: UN investigated 15 attacks on homes killing 216 people (115 children, 50 women). Found in multiple cases: no evidence of military target, or attacks grossly disproportionate.
Protected Persons and ObjectsMedical Facilities: Fourth Geneva Convention Article 18 mandates protection of hospitals. 73 medical facilities attacked. Amnesty found 'mounting evidence' of deliberate targeting—grave breach.
Fourth Geneva Convention Violations - Israeli ForcesArticle 33 (Collective Punishments): 'Collective penalties...prohibited.' Destruction of power plant causing shutdown of water, sewage, medical services for entire population constitutes collective punishment.
Customary International Humanitarian Law ViolationsProportionality: Civilian harm must not be excessive relative to military advantage. UN Commission found multiple attacks 'grossly disproportionate.' Rafah assault, power plant destruction clearly disproportionate.
UN Commission of Inquiry Findings (June 2015)Possible Crimes Against Humanity: Commission noted pattern and scale of attacks on civilians may constitute crimes against humanity, though refrained from definitive conclusion pending full investigation.
Specific Incident InvestigationsShuja'iya: Commission found indiscriminate use of artillery in area with civilian density three times that of Tel Aviv violated laws of war. Over 100 killed in 24 hours.
Protected Persons and ObjectsSchools and Cultural Property: 262 schools damaged/destroyed. Hague Convention protects cultural property; attacks must be militarily necessary. Evidence suggests many attacks lacked necessity.
Fourth Geneva Convention Violations - Israeli ForcesArticle 53 (Destruction of Property): 'Any destruction...prohibited, except where rendered absolutely necessary by military operations.' Destruction of 18,000 homes, power plant, medical facilities, schools far exceeded military necessity.
Customary International Humanitarian Law ViolationsPrecautions in Attack: Parties must take feasible precautions to minimize civilian harm. Despite 'roof knocking' and warnings, 551 children killed suggests inadequate precautions. Attacks on marked UN schools violated this.
UN Commission of Inquiry Findings (June 2015)War Crimes - Palestinian Armed Groups: Commission found indiscriminate rocket attacks and extrajudicial executions constituted war crimes under Common Article 3 and customary IHL.
Specific Incident InvestigationsRafah Black Friday: 1,000+ shells in 3 hours killing 130-150 (mostly civilians) found to be 'disproportionate in the extreme' and indicative of violations.
Protected Persons and ObjectsUN Facilities: UN marked facilities have special protected status. Multiple attacks on UNRWA schools despite coordination violated this protection.
Fourth Geneva Convention Violations - Israeli ForcesArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): 'Wilful killing...torture...wilfully causing great suffering...extensive destruction...not justified by military necessity' are grave breaches. Multiple documented incidents meet this threshold.
Customary International Humanitarian Law ViolationsIndiscriminate Attacks Prohibited: Use of imprecise artillery in densely populated areas (Shuja'iya, Rafah) constitutes indiscriminate attack. Palestinian rocket attacks also indiscriminate.
UN Commission of Inquiry Findings (June 2015)Accountability Failure: Commission found Israeli investigations 'inconsistent with international standards' and unlikely to produce genuine accountability. Palestinian authorities conducted no known investigations.
Specific Incident InvestigationsGaza Beach Boys: HRW investigation found killing of four boys on beach with no military target present indicative of war crime.
Protected Persons and ObjectsEssential Civilian Infrastructure: Additional Protocol I Article 54 prohibits attacks on objects indispensable to survival of civilian population. Power plant destruction violated this.
Specific Incident InvestigationsUN Facilities: Attacks on clearly marked UN schools sheltering displaced found to lack military justification; some attacks may constitute war crimes.

Commanders

1949-present Benjamin NetanyahuAuthorized Operation Protective Edge. Made key policy decisions including continuation despite international outcry. Defended operation as proportionate and necessary. Rejected UN Commission findings.
1950-present Moshe Ya'alonOversaw military planning and execution. Defended IDF actions including power plant destruction. Later expressed some regret about civilian toll but maintained operation was justified.
1959-present Benny GantzTop military commander during operation. Responsible for operational decisions including artillery use in Shuja'iya, Rafah assault. Later boasted about 'sending Gaza back to Stone Age.' Became Defense Minister 2020.
1962-present Ismail HaniyehHamas political leader during operation. Authorized continued rocket attacks throughout operation. Rejected ceasefire offers. Currently heads Hamas Political Bureau.
1965-present Mohammad DeifCommander of Hamas military wing. Directed rocket attacks and tunnel operations. Survived multiple Israeli assassination attempts including during this operation. Wife and children killed in airstrike August 19, 2014.
1945-present Mary McGowan DavisLed UN investigation into Operation Protective Edge. Former US federal judge. Commission documented violations by both sides, found evidence of war crimes.
